data.body_html:
Dolphin watching from a Marbella boat rental is one of the most magical experiences on the Costa del Sol. The Mediterranean waters here are home to several dolphin species, and with the right spot and timing, you can see them leaping alongside your yacht. Whether you're departing from Puerto Banús or exploring the coast, this guide covers the best spots for dolphin watching in Marbella, what to expect, and how to choose the right boat for your trip.

Why Marbella Is a Top Destination for Dolphin Watching

Marbella's coastline offers a unique mix of deep waters close to shore and rich feeding grounds. The waters off Estepona, Cabopino, and the Strait of Gibraltar are known for high dolphin activity. With water temperatures ranging from 14°C in winter to 28°C in summer, dolphins are present year-round but most visible from April to October. The area's marine biodiversity, including schools of fish and squid, attracts bottlenose, common, and striped dolphins. A boat rental in Marbella gives you access to these prime locations, away from crowded beaches.

Best Spots for Dolphin Watching Near Marbella

Here are the top locations for dolphin sightings, all reachable within 2-4 hours from Puerto Banús:

  • Estepona Coast (10 NM west): Known for resident bottlenose dolphins. Calm waters and clear visibility make it a favourite.
  • Cabopino (5 NM east): A protected area with rich marine life. Common dolphins are frequent here.
  • Strait of Gibraltar (30 NM west): A migration corridor for striped dolphins and pilot whales. Best for longer trips.
  • Sotogrande (20 NM west): Deep channels attract feeding dolphins, especially in the morning.
  • Cala del Faro (8 NM east): A quiet cove where dolphins often play near the rocks.

For the best experience, head out early (8-10 AM) or late afternoon (4-6 PM) when dolphins are most active feeding.

What Dolphins Can You See?

The most common species are bottlenose dolphins (up to 3.5m), common dolphins (up to 2.5m), and striped dolphins (up to 2.4m). Occasionally, you might spot pilot whales or even orcas during their migration in late summer. All sightings are wild and natural—no feeding or touching is allowed to protect the animals.

Best Boats for Dolphin Watching from Puerto Banús

Our fleet departs from Puerto Banús and includes options for every group size. For a 2-hour trip, the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) or Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) are ideal, both priced at €749 for 2 hours (skipper, drinks, snacks, and VAT included). For a longer adventure, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) offers a flybridge with panoramic views, starting at €4,719 for 4 hours (includes a free jet ski). Other boats like the Pershing 46 or Ferretti 94 are available on request via WhatsApp. All charters include a licensed skipper, fuel, insurance, and refreshments.

Tips for a Successful Dolphin Watching Trip

  • Book early morning or late afternoon for best sightings.
  • Bring binoculars and a camera with a zoom lens.
  • Wear sunscreen and a hat—the Mediterranean sun is strong.
  • Choose a boat with a flybridge for elevated views (e.g., Mangusta 80 or Azimut 58 Flybridge).
  • Listen to your skipper—they know the local hotspots.

Remember, dolphins are wild, so patience is key. Most trips see them within 30-60 minutes of reaching the right area.

Why Choose Boat Rental Marbella for Dolphin Watching?

We operate from Puerto Banús, the heart of Marbella's luxury marina. Our skippers have years of local experience and know exactly where to find dolphins. Every charter includes fuel, drinks, snacks, and insurance—no hidden costs. Whether you're celebrating a birthday or just want a unique day out, we have the perfect boat. Book your Marbella boat rental today and experience the thrill of dolphin watching on the Costa del Sol.

The best time is from April to October when the Mediterranean is calm and warm, with water temperatures between 20°C and 28°C. Dolphins are more active and visible during these months, especially in the early morning or late afternoon.

You can see bottlenose dolphins, common dolphins, and striped dolphins. Occasionally, you might spot pilot whales or even orcas during migration seasons. All are wild and free in their natural habitat.

For small groups, the Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39 (both €749 for 2 hours) are ideal. For larger parties, the Mangusta 80 (€4,719 minimum 4 hours) offers a flybridge for panoramic views. All boats depart from Puerto Banús.
